projects.title: Inspection reporting that survives dead zones
projects.summary: Field officers complete rail-yard inspections with no signal, and the reports and photos still land. A single-writer sync framework replaced an edit model that lost work.
projects.problem: The previous app lost edits and photos when a ramp lost connectivity, and stranded uploads retried forever after a failed acknowledgement.
projects.role: Owned the offline flow end to end: state model, sync engine, photo pipeline, and the recovery paths.
approach: Single-writer fact logs so one ramp's writes cannot interleave and lose another ramp's
Per-ramp store keys, which killed cross-ramp data loss
Recovery from lost-acknowledgement conflicts, stale-version mismatches, and retry loops
Resumable partial photo sync with per-slot persistence to stop duplicate uploads
projects.outcome: Edits and photos stop getting lost. Reports completed offline arrive once, without duplicates or stranded retries.

projects.title: Access control for a 75-endpoint inspection API
projects.summary: Role and facility permissions resolved on every request and enforced by one shared gate at every write path, so users only see and edit what their role and ramps allow.
projects.problem: Authorization rules were scattered and easy to bypass, with no audit trail of who could reach what.
projects.role: Designed and built the role and facility access model, the shared request gate, the refusal error surface, and the access-assignment audit trail.
approach: Roles plus facility scoping, resolved per request rather than cached per session
One declarative gate on every portal and write endpoint
Machine-readable refusal errors following a standard problem-details format
Filterable audit trail of access changes
projects.outcome: Authorization lives in one contract instead of scattered checks, and every access change is attributable.

projects.title: Connecting mobile reports to a long-lived reporting system
projects.summary: A mobile inspection app submits reports into a decades-old reporting pipeline through a message queue, serving both automated machine submissions and officers' manual submissions on separate audience-scoped endpoints.
projects.problem: Two very different submission flows needed to share one service without forking the logic, and duplicate resubmissions had to be rejected.
projects.role: Built the integrated submission endpoint, image ingest, queue submission, report editing, and the de-duplication gate.
approach: Split OAuth audiences so machine and human callers cannot share a token path
Report edit and de-duplication so resubmissions are not counted twice
Direct coordination with the pipeline owner so the integration fit the existing setup
projects.outcome: One service carries both flows, and the downstream system receives clean, deduplicated reports.

projects.title: Taking an inspection app from one phone platform to both
projects.summary: Stood up the second mobile platform from scratch: toolchain, builds, deployment to test devices, and the two failures that only appeared on managed corporate devices.
projects.problem: The app worked in the emulator but failed on corporate-network devices, and a previous user's sign-in session survived sign-out and blocked the next user.
projects.role: Owned the rollout end to end, including build signing, same-day redeploys, and driving the fix with the security and device-management teams.
approach: Traced certificate failures with the security and network teams to a missing corporate root trust, fixed with a network security configuration
Found and fixed the single sign-on session that outlived sign-out
Same-day bug fixes and redeploys so testers were never blocked
projects.outcome: The app runs on both platforms on managed devices, with a rollout that never left testers waiting.

projects.title: Supervised automation that a human still approves
projects.summary: A competition runner where an AI agent plans each step, deterministic scripts do all the screen work, and the operator approves every write before it happens.
projects.problem: Agentic automation is only safe in a live operational setting when a person stays in the loop and every action is recoverable.
projects.role: Top contributor, 68 of 97 team commits: built the agent run layer, the live operator console, the run journals, and the documentation.
approach: Hash-chained run journals so an interrupted run can be recovered and audited
Plan-digest approval: the operator approves what the agent intends to do, before it writes
Deterministic scripts own all screen work, so the agent never improvises against production
Stop controls and a test suite that reached 940-plus passing tests
projects.outcome: Two full scenarios ran with zero halts, retries, or unplanned operator interventions, inside the time target for the combo scenario.

projects.title: Helping a team adopt AI-assisted engineering
projects.summary: Authored the shared rules, commands, and review practices that define how AI coding tools are used across the codebase, and turned review findings into permanent team rules.
projects.problem: AI tools produce inconsistent quality unless the team standardizes how they are driven, reviewed, and constrained.
projects.role: Authored the repository-level standards, a skill plugin with 21 agents and skills, and the confirmation gate used before review findings are posted or fixed.
approach: Every fix-and-review round produces a retrospective that encodes the missed finding as a standing rule
Secret scanning before commit and subagent scope discipline as global governance
Spec-guided development: contracts regenerated from source, test plans rendered from requirements
projects.outcome: One shared set of standards across the team, with 30-plus rules extracted from real review rounds and 500-plus AI coding sessions on record.

projects.title: Graph search over real-world datasets
projects.summary: Final project for the data structures course: a reusable C++ graph library and a search pipeline run against a real dataset, with the whole thing driven by CMake so it builds like the course projects.
projects.problem: The project had to turn a large real-world dataset into a weighted graph and answer reachability and shortest-path style questions on it efficiently.
projects.role: Team member with Aashish Subramanian, Ved Eti, and Soumil Gupta. Built the graph class and the traversal and search layer.
approach: Graph class supporting the textbook structures behind lists, trees, and graph search
Dataset ingestion from CSV into the graph model
Traversal and search solving the assignment's computational questions
CMake build matching the course machine-problem workflow
Maintained the course's Fall 2022 release repository for the term
projects.outcome: Final grade A in the course; the project solved the assigned dataset questions on top of the shared graph library.

projects.title: A database-backed app over public crime data
projects.summary: Team final project for the database systems course: a web application over the Los Angeles crime dataset, designed from an entity-relationship model through normalized schema to a working query surface.
projects.problem: The team had to model a large public dataset relationally, normalize it, and serve useful queries from a web front end without exposing raw data dumps.
projects.role: Team member. Worked the data model and query layer for the web application.
approach: Entity-relationship modeling of the crime dataset
Normalized relational schema with functional dependencies respected
Query design for the search and browse surface
JavaScript web front end over the database
projects.outcome: Final grade A in the course; the working app answered the assigned queries over the dataset.

projects.title: A small operating system kernel in C
projects.summary: The course project, extended into a standing repository: a kernel with a dynamic memory allocator, page-table system calls, a simple file system, and the device drivers the course specifies.
projects.problem: The kernel had to virtualize memory and devices with no modern OS safety net: allocation, paging, file access, and input and output all had to work in C at the system level.
projects.role: Sole author of the repository work, following the course's OS project specification.
approach: Dynamic memory allocator tracking free pages, with a malloc system call that adds pages to a program's page table
File system with an open system call for access
System call path followed end to end, the way the course's OS project requires
Demo-able functionality so the memory and file work could be shown, not assumed
projects.outcome: Final grade B+ in the course; the repository carries the allocator, file system, and syscall work with documentation.

projects.title: Pac-Man running on an FPGA
projects.summary: The classic arcade game implemented on an AMD Spartan-7 FPGA around a MicroBlaze soft-CPU system-on-chip, written in SystemVerilog with the game logic in C.
projects.problem: The game had to run as a hardware/software co-design: real peripherals, real timing, and a soft processor coordinating game state, display, and input on one chip.
projects.role: Sole author. Owned the SoC platform, the SystemVerilog, and the C game layer.
approach: MicroBlaze soft-CPU system-on-chip built through the platform configurator
SystemVerilog for the digital hardware layer
C for the game logic running on the soft CPU
Peripherals wired through the FPGA development board
projects.outcome: Final grade A+ in the course, the top mark in the term; the repository documents the full co-design.

projects.course: CS 444 Deep Learning for Computer Vision and CS 441 Applied Machine Learning, Spring 2024
projects.title: Self-supervised learning and object detection
projects.summary: A two-part machine learning project in PyTorch: training a model to predict image rotation with no labels as a self-supervised task on CIFAR-10, then transferring what it learned into object detection.
projects.problem: Labels are expensive. The project tested how much supervision a model actually needs by pretraining on a task the data provides for free, then transferring it.
projects.role: Sole author, built during deep learning and applied machine learning coursework.
approach: Self-supervised rotation prediction on CIFAR-10 with a ResNet-18 backbone
Transfer of the pretrained representation into a detection objective
PyTorch throughout, matching the coursework toolchain
projects.outcome: Final grades A+ in both courses in the term; the repository documents both parts of the project.

figures.label: final grades in CS 441 and CS 444

projects.title: NoteHub, a note-sharing app for students
projects.summary: A web app where college students open-source their notes for others: authentication, search, comment threads, and note uploads, with images stored as links rather than blobs to keep the client light.
projects.problem: Course notes are scattered and personal; the app set out to make them a shared resource with real account handling and search.
projects.role: Co-built with Lohit Muralidharan. Worked the web application layer.
approach: React and TypeScript front end
Django REST for authentication and serialization, Node and Express for uploads and comments
Firebase for free-tier storage tooling, with images referenced as links instead of stored blobs
SQLite for the relational data
projects.outcome: Working application with the full stack wired together.

projects.title: MetaGlasses, a phone-to-lens assistant
projects.summary: A wearable assistant pairing: a backend that handles the assistant's requests and a phone-side client, built with a FastAPI service and a TypeScript front end, plus a maintained API test collection.
projects.problem: A glanceable assistant needs a thin client and a careful API boundary: the phone sends, the service reasons and answers, and the contract between them has to stay testable.
projects.role: Sole author. Owns the backend, the API contract, and the client.
approach: FastAPI backend in Python with a TypeScript client
A Postman collection kept as the source of truth for the API contract
Test and model-response repositories supporting the contract work
projects.outcome: Working service and client with a documented, tested API surface.

projects.title: Pocket Greenhouse, a Roblox farming slice
projects.summary: An idle-farming vertical slice on Roblox written in Luau: a tight playable loop of planting, growing, and harvesting, with its own tooling repository.
projects.problem: Roblox projects need game feel and iteration speed; the slice is a complete loop rather than a feature demo.
projects.role: Sole author. Owns the game code and the tooling.
approach: Luau game code implementing the full idle-farming loop
A separate tooling repository for the build and iteration workflow
Kept private during development
projects.outcome: A playable vertical slice with the core loop complete.
